passage:
A student used an image from a museum website in a report but forgot to give credit. Her teacher asked her to correct it.
The student said, "But I did not steal the real painting."
The teacher explained that digital images also require respect. Museums, photographers, and researchers work to make them available. Credit helps others find the source and honors the work behind the image.
The student added proper information and learned how to cite sources.
The lesson was small but important. In the digital world, taking something may not remove it from its place, but it can still ignore ownership, labor, and trust.

glossary.translation: 可取得的；可使用的；有空的
